newsitem.title: USA: 39 men apparently kill selves in California.
newsitem.headline: 39 men apparently kill selves in California.

text.p: In an apparent mass suicide, 39 young men dressed alike and lying on their backs were found dead on Wednesday in a luxury mansion.

San Diego Sheriff's Capt. Alan Fulmer told reporters the cause of death was unknown as yet, but there was no blood or sign of trauma at the scene in Rancho Santa Fe, some 20 miles (32 km) north of San Diego.
He said the men, all 18 to 24 years old, were similarly dressed in dark pants and dark tennis shoes, although he did not describe their shirts.
He said the bodies were found on their backs with hands at their sides in different rooms of the mansion on a $1.6 hillside million estate located in a wealthy neighbourhood.
Acting on an anonymous tip, sheriff's deputies had gone to the house to investigate.

"Two deputies entered, they made their observation, they checked it out and then they backed out," he said, adding that there was no one alive in the house. He also said there was a pungent odour in the house.
Earlier, Sgt. Don Crist said the deputies initially found 10 bodies then "They lost count at 10."
Lt. Gerald Lipscomb, also of the Sheriff's Department, said there no suicide note. There was no immediate comment on whether the men were members of a religious cult.
"We don't know anything about them at this point," he said.
However, broadcast reports quoted neighbours as saying the people who rented the house, with a tennis court and swimming pool, were involved in some kind of religious activity.
One neighbour Bill Strong was quoted by CNN as saying the mansion was owned by a man named Sam Koutchessahani, who had rented it to people "from out of state" in October.
He said the people who lived in the house were "middle-aged, men and women, with out-of-state (license) plates." He had waved at them, but had no conversations.
But investigators said they did not know who owned the building.
The incident comes four days after a cult suicide in Saint Casimir, Quebec.
Five members of a notorious doomsday cult -- the Solar Temple -- died in a blazing house on Saturday in an apparent ritual suicide pact, Quebec police said.
And in 1994 and 1995, 69 members of the Solar Temple cult died in fires in Canada and Switzerland.
